UGWPv1 under MPAS — isolated gravity-wave-drag signal (no gravity-wave vs. gravity-wave)¶

Run 10: do_ugwp_v1 = .false. and do_ugwp_v1_w_gsldrag = .false. — the true no-gravity-wave-drag control. (Setting only do_ugwp_v1 = .false. is not enough: GFS_typedefs.F90:5430-5439 force-sets the three do_gsl_drag_* flags from do_ugwp_v1_w_gsldrag regardless of do_ugwp_v1, so the first baseline attempt still had full orographic drag active — see run10's stress fields below, confirmed exactly zero.)

Run 11: do_ugwp_v1 = .true. and do_ugwp_v1_w_gsldrag = .true.

Both runs: x1.40962 mesh (120 km, 40962 cells, 59 levels), dt = 720 s, init 2023-03-10 15Z, forecast to 03Z (12 h), output at 3-hour intervals.

Helpers¶

3. Where the drag acts: surface stress maps (run 11, end of forecast)¶

Vertically integrated momentum flux by branch: ls = mesoscale orographic gravity waves, bl = low-level flow blocking, fd = turbulent orographic form drag (Beljaars). ss (small-scale GW) is exactly zero throughout — gated on hpbl, which is a clear (unset) value because this suite has no PBL scheme.

4. The isolated GWD signal — deceleration test¶

For each cell/level, project the wind-vector change. Negative = gravity-wave drag decelerating the flow relative to the no-drag control. Grouped by the mesoscale-orography roughness (var2dls) and by height above the local terrain, so this isolates the orographic branches' footprint from anything happening aloft (the non-orographic wave branch, which launches from 275 hPa).

height 0-1.5 km AGL 1.5-5 km 5-15 km
mean along-flow change at 3h (m/s)

5. Time evolution — low-level wind speed over rough vs. smooth terrain¶

The clearest single summary: mean wind speed in the lowest 1.5 km, averaged over cells with little subgrid orography (var2dls 0-50 m, GWD should do almost nothing) vs. cells with a lot (500-3000 m, GWD should visibly slow the flow). The two categories start identical (same initial condition) and diverge only in the run with GWD turned on.

12h low-level wind, rough terrain: 7.90 m/s (no GWD) -> 5.11 m/s (GWD)  (-35.3%)
12h low-level wind, smooth terrain: 9.35 m/s (no GWD) -> 9.27 m/s (GWD)  (-0.9%)

6. Map of the 12 h fingerprint¶

Low-level (0-1.5 km) wind-speed change, run 7 minus run 10, at the end of the forecast. If this is real orographic drag, the pattern should sit on the mountains (Alps, Andes, Rockies/coastal ranges, Tibet/Himalaya margins, Antarctic coastal escarpment) and be small over the oceans and plains.

7. Vertical structure — where the tendency acts¶

RMS of the 3-D wind tendency by height, split by branch. The orographic branches (ls, bl, fd) should be confined near the surface; the total (dtaux3d, includes the non-orographic CIRES branch) should also show a separate peak near the model top, from waves launched at 275 hPa breaking near the lid.

Summary¶

  • The gravity-wave-drag momentum path works, and this is now a clean same-code-version comparison. Run 10 (no GWD) and run 11 (GWD on) both use the post-rebase executable. This control the drag produces a physically located, terrain-graded deceleration: negligible over smooth terrain (var2dls 0-50 m: -0.1 m/s at 12 h), growing to -1.6 m/s in 3 hours and -3.3 m/s in 12 hours over the roughest terrain in the mesh (var2dls 500-3000 m), 83-87% of those cells decelerating, and concentrated in the lowest 1.5 km as expected for orographic drag. Surface stress peaks at 3.4 Pa total (ls 2.3 Pa, fd 2.2 Pa, bl 0.4 Pa; ss is exactly zero everywhere — gated on hpbl, which is unset because this suite has no PBL scheme), and the 12 h low-level wind speed over rough terrain falls from 7.9 to 5.1 m/s (-35%) versus essentially no change (-0.9%) over smooth terrain.
  • Not GWD: the top-of-model cooling and the slow global-mean surface-pressure drift are effectively identical with GWD on or off (theta change -6.50 K vs -6.49 K; ps drift -0.332 vs -0.335 hPa over 12 h) — both pre-exist this work and should be investigated separately.
  • Amplitude still looks too strong. The peak 3-D tendency is 1696 m/s/day (mesoscale/ls branch), and a 35% low-level wind-speed reduction over rough terrain in 12 hours remains well above typical NWP tuning targets (order 10%/day) — both numbers essentially unchanged from the pre-rebase runs, confirming the rebase didn't change the scheme's behavior, only fixed unrelated bugs. cdmbgwd = 0.14, 1.8 are unmodified C96 defaults; the missing theta/sigma/gamma/elvmax anisotropy fields (blocking/TOFD depth currently derived only from 2*hprime) may also be over-contributing. Both are the natural next things to adjust, now that there is a same-code-version GWD-on/GWD-off pair to measure any change against.
